Subject: MAP: POC environment — access gating, IP allowlist, and peering owners

Alex / infra team — attaching the initial MAP page for the POC so we can align on acceptance gates and the environment handoff. Key items we need to close this week: API key creation and scoping, Redwood org onboarding, IP allowlist for test & staging, and VPC peering timing (if you want peering instead of IP allowlist for the staging cluster).

Action ask (today):
- Please confirm a primary infra contact for VPC peering (name + email).
- Send the IP ranges you intend to use for the test subnet if peering is not needed.
- Confirm whether HealthGrid will accept a staging-only API key (scoped to test dataset) or needs production-equivalent credentials for load testing.

I've attached: MAP_draft_v1.pdf (high level milestones), network_manifest.csv (expected ports/protocols), and a small sample ip list file we use as a template. Once we have your contact and ranges I'll open the peering request and schedule the first traffic smoke-test.

If helpful I can schedule a short 30-min tech sync tomorrow to walk the runbook.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0191

Attachments: MAP_draft_v1.pdf (3 pages), network_manifest.csv (stub), healthgrid_ip_ranges.txt (stub)

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@healthgrid.com>

Cc: ops+infra@healthgrid.com, procurement@healthgrid.com
Date: Mon, 26 Nov 2028 09:01:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: MAP: POC environment — access gating, IP allowlist, and peering owners

Grace — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers:
- Primary peering contact: Priya Dutta (pri.dutta@healthgrid.com). I'll loop her in below.
- For the initial POC we prefer IP allowlist for the test cluster (faster), then evaluate peering for scale tests. I'll attach our current CIDR blocks in a follow-up.
- Regarding API keys: procurement will want scoped test keys first. We'll request production-equivalent credentials only for the final acceptance run.

Can you confirm what ports/protocols Redwood needs open for the ephemeral test agents? I see the CSV but want an explicit line I can paste into our firewall ticket. Also please confirm your suggested cutover window to avoid impacting our nightly ETL.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Rivera
Director, Infrastructure — HealthGrid
alex.rivera@healthgrid.com

Folks — I updated the MAP to include two acceptance gates (connectivity smoke, end-to-end scenario run). See attached MAP_v2.pdf. Notable changes:
- We require an "allowlist confirmation" step (HealthGrid provides CIDRs; Redwood validates connectivity by 2 iperf checks and a token-exchange).
- API keys: create a read/write test key and a read-only key for monitoring. Notes in the doc on TTL and rotation.
- If peering is chosen later, add a "routing validation" checklist (route propagation + NAT behavior).

Jonas — can you draft the firewall ticket payload (one-liner entries for their SRE to paste) and add to the network_manifest.csv? Karthik, I put an item for you to validate the token scoping rules so procurement can sign off.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Manager, Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: MAP: POC environment — access gating, IP allowlist, and peering owners

Alex / Priya — putting the allowlist entries for your firewall ticket below (one-line clipboard friendly). We tested these against our staging agents:

# Redwood staging egress (source) -> HealthGrid test endpoints (dest):
- Source: 34.72.144.0/24; Destination: <your-test-subnet-cidr>; Ports: 443 (HTTPS), 8443 (gRPC)
- Source: 34.72.145.0/24; Destination: <your-test-subnet-cidr>; Ports: 53 (DNS outbound) - UDP

If you prefer a single rule block we can also provide a /23 range. For the token-exchange handshake we use outbound 443 to healthgrid-auth.healthgrid.internal:443 (TLS) only.

Regarding peering: if you schedule peering we will need a VPC ID and route table to test propagation (we can do a 1-hour window for route validation).
